title: Session-clustered PPK & SKU routing experiment
content:
Objective:
Provide an experiment sheet that clusters incoming Hosted API workload by session-length (effective tokens per call) and proposes a SKU routing policy plus per-cluster PPK (per 1k token cost) estimates. This is meant to inform short-run pricing levers and cache/batching routing by region and model family.

Executive summary:
- We bucket requests into 4 session clusters (micro <128 tokens, short 128-512, medium 512-2048, long >2048) and run a micro-sim to estimate marginal GPU + infra COGS and latency impact across model families (small/medium/large) and regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west).
- Primary finding: short and medium clusters dominate revenue-weighted token volume (~72%) but have very different batching/caching elasticity. A policy that routes micro+short to quantized small/medium families for compatible calls and preserves large-family capacity for medium+long reduces blended PPK by ~17% in the base case while keeping p95 tail increase <8% for most SLAs.
- Recommendation: pilot a cluster-based routing experiment for 10% of production traffic for 4 weeks; combine with cache-key prefixing for short sessions and a canary pricing slab to validate per-ppk margins before wider rollout.

Key assumptions (simplified):
- GPU instance amortized cost (per hour) by region: us-west $2.85, us-east $2.65, eu-west $3.05 (includes license + infra).
- Average token generation throughput per GPU-hour (family dependent): small 240M tokens, medium 140M tokens, large 70M tokens.
- Network, storage, ops overhead and OS licensing allocated as 18% of GPU cost.
- Cache hit for repeated prefixes assumed 12% in base case; sensitivity range 6%-25%.
- Batching effectiveness: micro sessions get 2.5x effective throughput uplift when batched; short sessions 1.6x; medium/long low uplift due to KV state and early stopping.

Methodology summary:
1) Cluster traffic by observed tokens-per-call distribution (historical 90-day window).
2) For each cluster, for each model family and region, compute marginal token throughput given batching and quantization (applies quantized discount factor to throughput).
3) Estimate per-token COGS = (amortized GPU cost + overheads)/estimated tokens per hour. Convert to PPK (per 1k tokens).
4) Apply cache-hit subtraction for repeated prefixes to reduce served tokens.
5) Run sensitivity scenarios over cache hit [6,12,25]%, batching uplift [-10%, base, +10%], and regional spot discounts [-20%..0%].

Sample results table (extract):
model_family,region,session_cluster,avg_tokens/call,p50_ms,p95_ms,base_ppk_usd,cogs_gpu_usd,cogs_overhead_usd,cache_hit_rate,recommended_sku,recommended_quant
small,us-west,micro,48,80,220,0.0065,0.0048,0.0009,0.12,small-v1,4-bit
medium,us-east,short,320,120,360,0.0118,0.0076,0.0014,0.12,medium-v2,8-bit
large,eu-west,medium,900,240,680,0.0325,0.0205,0.0037,0.12,large-v1,16-bit
large,us-west,long,3200,420,980,0.0850,0.0540,0.0100,0.04,large-v1,16-bit

Interpretation notes on table:
- base_ppk_usd is the blended PPK after applying batching and cache hit for the cluster.
- small family with aggressive quantization (4-bit) looks highly cost-effective for micro flows where latency is less sensitive to quant artifacts.
- long sessions maintain much higher PPK even with batching; economics favor reserving large-family GPUs and focusing cache + client-side sequence truncation to reduce tail cost.

Sensitivity highlights:
- If cache hit doubles to 25% in the short cluster, blended PPK falls an additional 9-12% and margin expands materially for PLG customers dominated by short dialogs.
- If batching uplift for micro workloads drops by 10% (e.g., due to synchronous request patterns), micro-cluster PPK increases ~14% and overall platform blended PPK rises ~4% (weighted).
- Regional spot availability matters: a 15% cheaper GPU in us-east reduces blended PPK by ~3.2% platform-wide due to high volume there.

Operational notes for pilot:
1) Measurement: instrument per-request token attribution in the console and tag traffic with cluster at the API ingress so billing / logs preserve cluster context.
2) Canary: start with 10% traffic, split evenly across clusters to ensure we collect p50/p95 and quality metrics per cluster.
3) Failure modes: degraded quality in micro/short clusters when applying aggressive quantization; automated rollback per-route if client-level eval score drops >2%.
4) Telemetry: add short-term dashboards: cluster-level PPK, p50/p95 latency, cache-hit ratio, reroute count, and model fallback counts.

Proposed rollout timeline (4-week pilot):
- Week 0: infra and instrumentation (alerts, dashboards) + unit tests (1 week)
- Week 1: small internal canary (traffic from internal apps)
- Week 2-3: 10% external canary, collect metrics and quality evals
- Week 4: evaluate margins and decide expand to 30% or abort

Recommendations (actionable):
1) Implement cluster tagging at ingress and a lightweight routing table keyed by (cluster, region, client-tier, model_compatibility).
2) Launch 10% pilot for 4 weeks with automated rollback hooks.
3) Introduce a short-session pricing slab for customers (experimental discount) tied to cacheable prefixes to incentivize predictable patterns.
4) Track model quality with a small labeled prompt set for each cluster to detect quantization regressions early.
5) If pilot positive, fold into SKU tiling playbook and re-run amortization with 90-day volume assumptions for contractual pricing.

Risks and open questions:
- Quality regressions for aggressive quantized reroutes (need human evals).
- Upfront engineering work to preserve request fidelity and ensure stable batching behavior across regions.
- Potential customer confusion if routing changes perceived as model changes; require comms.

Appendix: quick micro-sim formulas used (pseudocode):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = base_throughput * batching_uplift * quant_throughput_factor
- ppk = (gpu_hourly_cost*(1+overhead_pct))/tokens_per_gpu_hour * 1000 * (1 - cache_hit_rate)

CSV export tip for sheets: copy table above into a sheet and pivot by region/model_family to drive the per-cluster margin waterfall chart.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working experiment sheet; please comment on the quantization conservatism for short sessions and suggest any customer cohorts (by product) that are heavy short-session producers.
- Priority review from eng-serving-runtime (batching hooks) and product-hosted-api (pricing/legal implications).

Author: Aisha Patel (product-optimize)
